Dataset: Customer Sentiment/Intent (sports e-commerce, 3-class: Positive_Praise, Negative_Complaint, Urgent_Support) -- expanded, N=452
Notes: EXP-05C + optimizer Adam->SGD (only change, same LR=0.005). Training essentially failed: EarlyStopping triggered after only 4/20 epochs (best weights from epoch 1) with F1 0.4184, barely above chance for 3 classes. Key finding for Discussion Q1 (code-based control vs no-code automation): a learning rate tuned for Adam is far too small for vanilla SGD, since Adam adapts step size per-parameter and SGD does not -- the same LR value means something very different depending on optimizer choice, a distinction a no-code tool hides entirely.

Notes: Isolates EXP-05D's capacity increase (hidden_dim 128) from its data expansion: same architecture as EXP-05D but trained on the ORIGINAL (non-expanded) dataset. Result: F1 0.8205, higher than EXP-05D's 0.7955 despite the smaller dataset -- on this split, the capacity increase interacts less favorably with the added rows than expected. Caveat: this run's validation set is smaller (50 vs EXP-05D's 68 examples), so the comparison is suggestive, not conclusive (Discussion Q3).

Smaller batches (more gradient noise per step) modestly helped generalization on this expanded dataset. Essentially tied with EXP-05G (0.8407) and EXP-05F (0.8390) -- treat as a top cluster of three rather than one decisive winner, but 05J posts the single highest F1 and precision.
